purpose: Trace each source/case from the provided Mega Drive video-derived material to accepted techniques, canonical skills, contracts, validators and deferred claims.
traceability_policy: Every accepted technique must have at least one owner skill.
Every owner skill must map to a contract, workflow, validator check or evidence requirement.
Every indirect or aggregate claim must remain scoped by the source reliability rubric.
Rejected or deferred claims must be explicit so future agents do not reintroduce them as canon.

sources.source_summary: 16 Tile workflow for Mega Drive tilemaps with per-cell palette, priority and H/V flip metadata.

accepted_techniques.description: Use 16-bit tile descriptors to encode priority, palette, H-flip, V-flip and tile index per cell.
Protect indexed palette ordering and transparency behavior before SGDK import.

rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: Tool export still requires SGDK resource integration, VDP budget and runtime evidence.

sources.source_summary: 16-bit sprite architecture: SAT/OAM, 4bpp indexed pixels, scanline limits, priority, flips and palette selection.

accepted_techniques.description: Budget sprite count and sprite pixels per scanline, not just total sprites on screen.
Sprites must respect 4bpp indexed color, transparency index and palette ownership.
evidence_required: human visual review for AAA sprite claims

rejected_or_deferred_claims.claim: A visually plausible sprite sheet proves runtime suitability
rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: Sprite sheets require palette, alignment, scanline, SAT and emulator evidence.

sources.source_summary: Mega Drive VDP tricks: line scroll, column scroll, H-Interrupt palette effects, dithering/composite transparency and raster-style effects.

accepted_techniques.description: Use Mega Drive-native Shadow/Highlight and scroll effects as explicit hardware strategies, not alpha blending.
Treat H-Interrupt palette changes and checkerboard dithering as constrained visual effects with display-mode caveats.
still_required_for_production: VDP/CRAM dump for mid-frame palette claim

rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: Mega Drive has Shadow/Highlight and display tricks, not generic alpha blending.
Mega Drive requires line scroll, software tile rasterization or pre-rendered approximations.

sources.source_summary: Comparison of classic assembly/hardware workflows and modern SGDK/rescomp/emulator workflows.

accepted_techniques.description: Use SGDK C/rescomp workflows while retaining hardware evidence, SGDK 2.11 header checks and emulator validation.
accepted_techniques.phase4f_note: SGDK Setup + VS Code added as candidate wrapper-operation rules: workspace sdk/sgdk-2.11/ is the canonical toolchain, inherited GDK from another workspace is not canonical, environment must pass assert_agent_environment.ps1, and toolchain errors become explicit diagnostics.
still_required_for_production: emulator evidence when a ROM is delivered

rejected_or_deferred_claims.claim: Modern tooling removes need for hardware-budget validation
rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: SGDK improves productivity but does not remove VRAM, CRAM, DMA, SAT or emulator evidence constraints.

sources.source_summary: Mega Drive graphics pipeline: VRAM, CRAM, VSRAM, 8x8 tiles, descriptors, DMA and line-buffer rendering.

accepted_techniques.description: Treat VRAM, CRAM, VSRAM, DMA and tile descriptors as first-class production constraints.

rejected_or_deferred_claims.claim: Smooth gradients or high color without strategy
rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: Requires palette cycling, H-Int, Shadow/Highlight or other explicit hardware strategy plus evidence.
rejected_or_deferred_claims.note: high_color_illusion gate and high-color conversion flow added as candidate; real true color is still impossible and production needs screenshot plus VDP/CRAM evidence.
still_required_for_production: VDP/CRAM dump when the illusion depends on mid-frame state

sources.source_summary: Independent developer techniques: articulated sprites, Z80 audio separation, software-driven pseudo-3D and custom engines.

accepted_techniques.description: Build impressive large characters through linked parts, anchors, SAT order and entity dispatch.
accepted_techniques.phase4c_note: Modular ability system (static struct + function pointers, fixed slot array, no malloc/free) and C/SGDK header/struct/enum patterns added as candidate.

accepted_techniques.description: Separate audio driver/PCM risk to Z80 and bound CPU-rendered tile effects through dirty uploads and DMA budget.
accepted_techniques.phase4e_note: YM2612/FM perceptual role, SN76489/PSG noise-UI-impact-texture and PCM/DAC sample prep added as candidate; music architecture stays with xgm2-audio-director and custom driver with z80-pcm-custom-driver (handoff only).

rejected_or_deferred_claims.claim: Unbounded software 3D engine as general canon
rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: Accepted only as bounded software tile rasterizer guidance until a concrete project scope and budget exist.
rejected_or_deferred_claims.phase4d_note: Fake Mode 7 (line scroll/z-map/tile rewrite), rotozoom/fullscreen rotation, wireframe and simple solid triangles added as bounded candidate rules; OutRun-style road perspective stays owned by hscroll-linescroll-road-fx first.

sources.source_summary: Another agent's aggregate claim about 64 videos and summary counts.

accepted_techniques.description: Use the 20/15/14/8/3/2 counts as backlog and decision-matrix pressure, not as proof of individual source review.

rejected_or_deferred_claims.claim: All 64 videos were verified by this agent
rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: Only the material available in the thread is directly available; aggregate remains indirect evidence.

sources.source_summary: Another agent's aggregate plan summarizing additional Mega Drive AAA techniques and proposed skill changes.

rejected_or_deferred_claims.claim: The plan's proposed techniques and skill changes are canonical
rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: Aggregate textual summary with no per-technique source records, owners or evidence. Routed to video_curation_evidence_backlog for triage; maps to backlog, not to any ready skill. In Phase 4B, raster/scroll, Shadow/Highlight, palette cycling and high-color/true-color illusion concepts were absorbed as candidate operational rules into existing VDP/color owner skills; the aggregate as a whole remains backlog.

sources.source_summary: Direct text analysis of pixel-art character proportion for platformers (16x32, 3-4 head heights, baseline/feet, visual margin vs hitbox, 16x16 grid coherence) with illustrative C code.

accepted_techniques.description: Author platformer characters around a 16x32 proportion of 3-4 head heights with explicit baseline/feet and a visual margin distinct from the hitbox, coherent with the 16x16 grid. Recorded as direct text; expansion into the owner skills is deferred to Phase 4.
evidence_required: visual fixture showing the proportion at 16x32 in a real scene
baseline/feet contract reconciled with the collision hitbox
runtime screenshot or VDP dump for any visual-quality claim
still_required_for_production: visual fixture showing the proportion at 16x32 in a real scene
baseline contract reconciled with the collision hitbox

rejected_or_deferred_claims.claim: The attachment's example C code is a canonical API
rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: Illustrative C code does not become a canonical API.

rejected_or_deferred_claims.claim: Correct proportion proves AAA quality or runtime suitability
rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: Direct text analysis does not prove runtime; no testado_em_emulador, validado_budget or ready_for_aaa is implied. Owner-skill expansion is deferred to Phase 4.

sources.source_summary: Attached technical transcript about game music composition: adaptive music, seamless loops, vertical remixing, horizontal resequencing, middleware concepts and illustrative SGDK-style C.

accepted_techniques.description: Represent adaptive music as gameplay events routed to an audio director, which schedules state changes, priorities, fallbacks and channel ownership instead of letting scenes call raw music changes everywhere.
evidence_required: BlastEm evidence for runtime audio claims

accepted_techniques.description: Translate horizontal resequencing into BPM, time signature, NTSC/PAL frame timing, allowed transition points, stinger/bridge ids and missed-window fallback.
evidence_required: runtime proof before any delivery claim

accepted_techniques.description: Require each SFX/timbre to declare gameplay role, priority and coexistence with music before assigning FM, PSG or PCM resources.

rejected_or_deferred_claims.claim: FMOD/Wwise/RTPC behavior maps directly to Mega Drive
rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: Modern middleware concepts can inspire structure but must be translated to discrete states, supported fades, stingers, pre-rendered variants or custom-driver handoff.

rejected_or_deferred_claims.claim: Illustrative C code is canonical SGDK/XGM2 code
rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: The snippet is not validated against headers, contains patterns owned by input/debug/UI skills and is not runtime evidence.

rejected_or_deferred_claims.claim: Text analysis proves excellent or AAA audio
rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: E1_text can strengthen candidate rules only; production still needs contracts, real assets, auditory test, build and emulator evidence.

sources.source_summary: Attached technical transcript about NES parallax via Sprite 0 hit, mapper scanline IRQs and translation of raster/line-split thinking to Mega Drive HSCROLL_LINE and pseudo-3D roads.

accepted_techniques.description: Treat NES Sprite 0/MMC3/PPUSCROLL details as historical analogy, then express the Mega Drive implementation through VDP mechanisms: HSCROLL_LINE, HSCROLL_TILE, WINDOW, H-Int or plane ownership.
evidence_required: BlastEm evidence for runtime motion claims

accepted_techniques.description: Before runtime, declare the visible bands or line ranges, plane owner, scroll ratio, horizon and fallback for banded or per-line parallax.
evidence_required: art authoring check for band readability

accepted_techniques.description: Pseudo-3D floor/road line scroll requires a horizon line, formula or LUT for ratios, update cadence, transfer method, gameplay camera source and cheaper fallback.

rejected_or_deferred_claims.claim: NES Sprite 0/MMC3 timing workflow is a Mega Drive implementation rule
rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: The Mega Drive has native VDP scroll modes and different interrupt/plane mechanisms; copying NES workflow would mislead implementation.

rejected_or_deferred_claims.claim: Line scroll creates unlimited independent layers
rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: Line scroll offsets rows/lines within an existing plane; it does not allocate new independent tilemaps or palettes.

rejected_or_deferred_claims.claim: Illustrative demo code proves a production-ready road/parallax engine
rejected_or_deferred_claims.reason: The snippet lacks art contract, budget, ownership, camera/input separation, fallback and emulator evidence.
